To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The free amino acid pool of the fetal brain is disturbed during the last trimester of gestation, and this disturbance is associated with the increased concentration of branched chain amino acid in the fetal serum, and 2) Isoleucine appears to have the greatest influence on the free amino acid content of the fetal brain.
“The elevated levels of the Branched chain amino acids (BCAA) were associated with a depression in the other amino acids of the free amino acids in fetal brain.
The free amino acid pool of the fetal brain is altered by the presence of high levels of branched chain amino acid, especially isoleucine, in fetal serum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of branched chain amino acid administration to the pregnant rat upon the free amino acid content of fetal brain.
the effect of branched chain amino acid on fetal development.
the effects of the maternal injection of the individual branched chain amino acid on the free amino acid levels of fetal rat brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the free amino acids of fetal brain were altered by the presence of elevated levels of isoleucine.
the branched chain acids, leucine, isoleucine, and valine are present in the brain and that these compounds are elevated in the brain during the period of rapid brain growth and development.
the free amino acids of the fetal rat brain are not in a steady state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
isoleucine is a very potent inhibitor of the incorporation of other amino acids into protein.
the amino acids in fetal brain are in a state of dynamic equilibrium with those in the serum.
the amino acids are not the same in the brain and the blood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is not a static organ, but is constantly changing in response to the environment and the needs of the individual.
the brain is not a passive recipient of amino acids, and that there are mechanisms in place that can actively regulate amino acid levels in the brain.
the free amino acids of the brain are in a state of dynamic equilibrium.
